extracted.intended_audience: general Indian readers of entertainment/current affairs news
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging a comedian's politically charged stand-up monologue (especially when performed/uploaded abroad) — including intent, audience reaction, legal risk, and concerns about generalisation or insult. Geared toward assessing controversies around such performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire about 'two Indias' (duality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The video is a satire about the duality of two very separate India's that do different things. Like any nation has light and dark, good and evil within it. None of this is a secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the piece frames contrasting aspects of the country as satire/duality rather than an outright denunciation; check that it acknowledges both 'light and dark' and intends critical reflection rather than wholesale condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intention to remind of the country's greatness
rubrics_metrics.description: The video appeals for us to never forget that we are great. To never stop focusing on what makes us great... It ends in a gigantic patriotic round of applause for a country we all love, believe in and are proud of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the performance ultimately affirms patriotism and national pride (e.g., ending in applause) and whether its critical content is framed as a call to remember positives rather than to denigrate the nation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of edited snippets / need for context
rubrics_metrics.description: Vir also asked everyone not to be fooled by edited snippets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not evaluate the piece solely on short, shared clips; ensure the full performance/context is considered before judging intent or content. Check for selective editing that could misrepresent the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reaction should convey hope/respect, not hate/malice
rubrics_metrics.description: People cheer for India with hope, not hate. People clap for India with respect, not malice. You cannot sell tickets, earn applause, or represent great people with negativity, only with pride.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging the reception, distinguish applause given as supportive patriotism from applause perceived as derision; consider stated or visible audience intent as part of evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of speech does not permit slander/generalisation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Your freedom of speech doesn't mean the slander of the male population of my country. Your generalisation is beyond shameful."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether critical remarks constitute defamatory slander or impermissible broad generalisations about groups (e.g., men, Hindus) rather than targeting specific behaviours or systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid insulting the motherland, especially when performed abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Several social media users including politicians have mocked Vir for insulting his motherland in a foreign country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the setting (performing abroad) when evaluating appropriateness; critics may view commentary delivered internationally as disloyal or inappropriate regardless of intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of legal/police complaint for allegedly derogatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: A police complaint has also been filed ... for allegedly using derogatory language against India during his performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that allegedly derogatory public statements can trigger formal complaints and potential legal consequences; include legal risk as part of the evaluation of a public monologue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage and public value in speaking uncomfortable truths
rubrics_metrics.description: "I come from an India where it needs courage for a Vir Das to say this... many of us admire this courage, yet choose to remain silent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance criticisms by considering whether the performance performs a valuable public service by raising issues others avoid; assess the social value of truth-telling and the bravery involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not target entire communities or conflate crime with culture
rubrics_metrics.description: "Why are these comedians & Bolywood gang after Hindus for worshiping Feminine? Their constant attempt 2 defame Hindus by linking every crime with Sanatan culture is a part of a bigger conspiracy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the monologue unjustly links criminal acts to a religion/culture or scapegoats an entire community; responsible satire should avoid implicating whole groups for societal problems.
